K-236.h1: Pre-Writing Tracing Lines: Loops, Waves, and Zigzags
K-236.title: Pre-Writing Tracing Lines for Preschool | Free Printable PDF
K-236.metaDescription: Free printable pre-writing worksheet: trace loops, waves and zigzag lines from the orange start dot to the waiting animal. Preschool tracing PDF.
K-236.p1: This Preschool pre-writing worksheet turns tracing lines into a little journey across the page. Each lane begins with a bright orange start dot and ends with a friendly animal waiting at the finish line. The child places their pencil on the dot, follows the arrow, and rides the loops, waves, and zigzags all the way over to the animal — one steady line per lane. There are no letters or numbers to worry about yet; the whole job is simply keeping the pencil on the path.
K-236.p2: Those curvy, bumpy paths are doing quiet but serious work. Loops, waves, and zigzags contain the very strokes that letters and numerals are built from, so tracing them develops pencil grip, hand strength, and the controlled changes of direction that handwriting demands. Traveling each lane from left to right also rehearses the direction English print flows, and the animal at the end gives even a reluctant three-year-old a real reason to finish every line.
K-236.p3: The worksheet prints free as a PDF, so it is easy to keep a fresh stack ready for warm-up minutes or quiet time. Once those lines feel smooth and confident, the same start-dot-and-arrow support carries straight into tracing the numbers 0 to 9, and from there into tracing capital letters — the natural next steps on the road to real handwriting.

K-237.h1: Number Tracing 0 to 9 on Writing Lines
K-237.title: Number Tracing 0-9 for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-237.metaDescription: Number tracing worksheet 0-9: solid models, dashed copies, orange start dots and stroke arrows on real writing lines. Free printable kindergarten PDF.
K-237.p1: This Kindergarten number tracing worksheet walks the child through writing every digit from 0 to 9. Each number sits on proper writing lines: first a solid model to look at, then a row of dashed copies to trace. A small orange dot marks exactly where the pencil starts, and little arrows show which way each stroke travels, so the child forms every numeral the correct way from the very first attempt.
K-237.p2: Stroke order matters more than it looks. Children who learn to start a 2 or a 5 in the right place write numbers faster, reverse them less often, and free up attention for the math itself. The dashed copies give just the right amount of support — the model shows what good looks like, the dashes guide the hand, and by the end of the row the child is writing the numeral nearly on their own.
K-237.p3: Print the PDF free and use one or two numbers a day rather than the whole page at once — short, correct practice beats long, tired practice every time. It pairs naturally with capital letter tracing for a full handwriting session, and once the digits feel secure, number bonds to 10 puts those freshly written numerals straight to work.

K-238.h1: Capital Letter Tracing on Handwriting Lines
K-238.title: Capital Letter Tracing for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-238.metaDescription: Capital letter tracing worksheet: trace six capitals on handwriting lines, then write each one alone in the empty slot. Free printable kindergarten PDF.
K-238.p1: This Kindergarten letter tracing worksheet puts six capital letters on real handwriting lines. For each letter the child traces the dashed models, feeling how the strokes sit between the lines — and then meets the best part: the last slot on every line is left empty, so they finish by writing the capital all on their own. No dashes, no help, just the letter they have just practiced. Six letters make a comfortable session for young hands — enough to feel real, short enough to end well.
K-238.p2: Capital letters are the friendliest place to start handwriting: they are big, they are built from simple straight and curved strokes, and they all stand the same height. Tracing builds the motor memory of each letterform, while the empty final slot turns tracing into genuine writing and shows both child and teacher instantly whether the shape has stuck. That trace-then-write rhythm is the same gradual release good handwriting programs are built on.
K-238.p3: The sheet prints free as a PDF, so it is easy to revisit the trickier letters as often as needed. For a rounded session, warm up first with pre-writing tracing lanes, and once the child writes letters confidently, sight word practice — read, trace, write — lets those capitals start spelling real words.

K-239.h1: Sight Words: Read, Trace, and Write
K-239.title: Sight Words Worksheet for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-239.metaDescription: Sight words worksheet: read, trace and write four high-frequency words on handwriting lines. Free printable kindergarten PDF for beginning readers.
K-239.p1: This Kindergarten sight words worksheet gives the child four high-frequency words and a simple three-step job for each: read the word aloud, trace it on the dashed model, then write it all by themselves on the empty line. That read–trace–write sequence keeps eyes, voice, and hand all working on the same word, one line at a time, until each of the four words has been read, traced, and written.
K-239.p2: Sight words are the little glue words — the ones that appear on nearly every page a child will ever read, and often the very ones that refuse to follow phonics rules. Moving them into instant memory matters because a reader who no longer sounds out common words has attention left over for what the sentence actually means. Saying the word anchors it in the ear, tracing anchors it in the hand, and writing it from memory proves it is starting to stick.
K-239.p3: Print the PDF free and treat it as a repeatable routine rather than a one-off: four words at a time is exactly the right dose. Capital letter tracing makes a good companion sheet while letter formation is still growing, and a short read-and-answer story is the perfect place for the child to meet their new words out in the wild.

K-240.h1: Cut and Paste: Sort the Animals into Their Boxes
K-240.title: Cut and Paste Sorting for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-240.metaDescription: Cut and paste sorting worksheet: cut out the animal pictures, sort them and glue each one into its labeled box. Free printable kindergarten PDF.
K-240.p1: This Kindergarten cut and paste worksheet ends with glue on fingers and a big smile. Along the bottom of the page runs a strip of animal pictures. The child cuts the strip apart, looks closely at each animal, decides which of the labeled boxes it belongs in, and glues it into place. Cutting, sorting, and pasting — three of childhood's favorite jobs, all on one page, with animals doing the starring roles.
K-240.p2: There is real learning hiding inside the fun. Steering scissors along a line is one of the best fine-motor workouts a young hand can get, building the same control that pencil work needs. And the sorting is early classification thinking: to place each animal, the child has to notice its features, compare it with the category labels, and commit to a decision. That look-compare-decide loop is the root of the grouping children later do in math and science.
K-240.p3: The worksheet prints free as a PDF — worth remembering, since a cut-up page can hardly be reused. When the scissors go back in the drawer, a color by code picture keeps the careful-looking practice going with crayons instead, and a maze offers the same happy mix of pencil control and puzzle.

K-241.h1: Color by Code: Solve the Sum, Match the Color
K-241.title: Color by Code for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-241.metaDescription: Color by code worksheet: solve the little sum inside each shape, check the color legend and color it to match. Free printable kindergarten math PDF.
K-241.p1: This Kindergarten color by code worksheet hides a math page inside a coloring page. Twelve outline shapes are scattered across the sheet, and each one holds a small addition problem. The child solves the little sum, checks the legend to see which color that answer calls for, and colors the shape to match. Solve, check the code, color — twelve times over, until every shape on the page has found its color.
K-241.p2: Color by code works because the coloring is the reward and the math is the price of admission — a price children pay happily. Every shape asks for one small computation and one careful match against the legend, so the page quietly delivers a dozen repetitions of early addition facts along with genuine attention-to-detail practice. Reading a legend is itself a skill: it is the same key-reading children will use later on maps, charts, and graphs. And because the code maps numbers to color words, a little reading practice rides along for free.
K-241.p3: Print the PDF free and let the crayons do the motivating. If the child loves the decoding feeling, number bonds to 10 gives the same addition facts a different outfit, and a cut, sort, and paste page swaps the crayons for scissors while keeping the careful looking.

K-242.h1: Maze Worksheet: Help the Animal Reach the Toy
K-242.title: Maze Worksheet for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-242.metaDescription: Printable maze worksheet: guide the animal from the top of the big maze down to the toy at the goal. Pencil control and planning. Free kindergarten PDF.
K-242.p1: This Kindergarten maze worksheet is one big puzzle with a story built in: a friendly animal waits at the top of the maze, and its goal — a toy from the toy-themed artwork — sits at the bottom. The child starts at the animal and draws one continuous path through the corridors, backing out of dead ends and trying a new turn until the pencil finally arrives at the prize. One page, one maze, one very satisfying finish.
K-242.p2: A good maze is patience training disguised as play. The child has to look ahead before committing the pencil, hold a plan in mind while drawing, and recover cheerfully when a corridor closes — which is problem solving in its purest early form. At the same time, steering a line through narrow passages without touching the walls is first-rate pencil control, the very same steadiness that handwriting will soon demand.
K-242.p3: The maze prints free as a PDF, so a wrong turn is never a tragedy — just print another. Children who enjoy the journey usually love pre-writing tracing lanes, which offer the same travel-the-path feeling with loops and waves, while a color by code picture rewards the same careful looking with crayons.

K-243.title: Number Bonds to 10 for Kindergarten | Free Printable PDF
K-243.metaDescription: Number bonds to 10 worksheet: complete six part-part-whole bonds by writing the missing number in the dashed circle. Free printable kindergarten PDF.
K-243.p1: This Kindergarten number bonds worksheet shows six part-part-whole bonds that all make 10. Each bond is a little diagram: the whole, 10, connected to its two parts — except that in every bond one circle has been left blank. The child reads the numbers that are given, works out what is missing, and writes it into the dashed circle to complete the bond. Six bonds, six missing pieces, one big idea.
K-243.p2: Knowing the pairs that make ten — 6 and 4, 7 and 3, 8 and 2 — is one of the most valuable pieces of number knowledge a young mathematician can own. The bond diagram makes the relationship visible: numbers are not just symbols in a row but wholes that break into parts and parts that come back together. Children who own these facts decompose numbers effortlessly later on, which is exactly what mental strategies like making ten are built from.
K-243.p3: Print the PDF free and revisit it until the pairs come without counting. When they do, mental math within 20 is the natural next stop — it is precisely where those bonds start paying off — and a color by code page offers the same fact practice wrapped in crayons.

G1-208.h1: Mental Math Within 20: Add and Subtract in Your Head
G1-208.title: Mental Math Within 20 for Grade 1 | Free Printable PDF
G1-208.metaDescription: Mental math worksheet within 20: twelve mixed addition and subtraction problems to solve in the head. Free printable Grade 1 PDF for fact fluency.
G1-208.p1: This Grade 1 mental math worksheet lines up twelve addition and subtraction problems within 20 and asks for no written working at all. The child reads each problem, solves it in their head, and writes just the missing number in the box. Some problems add, some subtract, and the mix keeps every line honest — twelve small victories on one quiet page.
G1-208.p2: Mental math within 20 is the engine room of elementary arithmetic. These are the facts that column methods, word problems, and eventually multi-digit work all lean on, and the goal is fluency: answers that arrive quickly and calmly, without finger counting. A mixed page like this one keeps the child genuinely reading each problem instead of settling into autopilot, and the missing-number format sneaks in early algebraic thinking about what makes an equation true.
G1-208.p3: The worksheet prints free as a PDF, so it works beautifully as a warm-up routine — same format, fresh effort, a few minutes a day. Children who hesitate on certain facts can step back to number bonds to 10 to rebuild the pairs underneath, while confident solvers are ready for fact family houses, where the same numbers show off their family ties. A calm minute of mental math each morning adds up faster than any single long session.

G1-209.h1: Fact Family Houses: Four Facts from Three Numbers
G1-209.title: Fact Families Worksheet for Grade 1 | Free Printable PDF
G1-209.metaDescription: Fact families worksheet: use the three numbers on each roof to write the four related addition and subtraction facts. Free printable Grade 1 PDF.
G1-209.p1: This Grade 1 fact families worksheet builds four little houses, each with three numbers sitting on its triangular roof. Those three numbers are a family — like 3, 5, and 8 — and the child's job is to write the four related facts that live inside the house: two additions and two subtractions, all made from the very same trio. Four houses, sixteen facts, one satisfying pattern.
G1-209.p2: Fact families teach one of arithmetic's most powerful secrets: addition and subtraction undo each other. A child who sees that 3 + 5 = 8 also carries 8 − 5 = 3 in their pocket suddenly owns twice as many facts with no extra memorizing — and, more importantly, starts thinking in relationships instead of isolated sums. The house-and-roof picture keeps the trio visually anchored while the child works, which is exactly the support first graders need while the idea is new.
G1-209.p3: Print the PDF free and talk through the first house together — once the pattern clicks, children usually race through the rest. Mental math within 20 is the perfect companion page for putting those related facts to work at speed, and picture word problems show where the whole family turns up in real-life stories.

G1-210.h1: Number Words: Match the Numeral to the Word
G1-210.title: Number Words Worksheet for Grade 1 | Free Printable PDF
G1-210.metaDescription: Number words worksheet: read each numeral and circle the written number word that matches it. Free printable Grade 1 PDF for math and reading practice.
G1-210.p1: This Grade 1 number words worksheet shows six numerals, and beside each one three written number words. Only one of the words matches the numeral; the child reads all three carefully and circles the correct one. Six numbers, six careful decisions — a reading task and a math task rolled into one tidy page, with no writing required beyond the pencil circle itself. The gentle format makes it a favorite for morning work and early finishers alike.
G1-210.p2: Reading number words fluently is a small skill with a long reach. Word problems, math directions, forms, calendars — written numbers appear everywhere, and children need to connect fourteen the word with 14 the numeral as automatically as they connect a picture with its name. The multiple-choice format earns its keep here: the wrong options are close enough that the child must genuinely read every word, which catches the classic mix-ups like thirteen versus thirty before they have a chance to settle in.
G1-210.p3: The sheet prints free as a PDF and makes a tidy five-minute station where literacy meets math. It sits especially well beside counting coins, where amounts get read and written in a money context, and picture word problems, where number words appear inside real sentences that need solving.

G1-211.h1: Counting Coins: How Much Is in Each Purse?
G1-211.title: Counting Coins Worksheet for Grade 1 | Free Printable PDF
G1-211.metaDescription: Counting coins worksheet: count the coins in six purses and write each total amount in the box. Free printable Grade 1 money math PDF for coin practice.
G1-211.p1: This Grade 1 counting coins worksheet opens six little purses, each holding a handful of familiar coins. The child counts up the value of the coins in every purse — ideally starting from the biggest coin and counting on from there — and writes the total amount in the box beside it. Six purses, six totals, and plenty of honest counting in between.
G1-211.p2: Money is the friendliest real-world use of number a first grader knows. Counting mixed coins is genuinely demanding: the child must recognize each coin, recall its value, and switch skip-counting gears mid-stream — tens, then fives, then ones. That flexible counting is superb number-sense exercise, and because the coins are the very ones children see in real life, the skill transfers straight to piggy banks, allowances, and pretend shops at home. Writing each total in the box also gives early practice in recording money amounts correctly, a small habit with a long life.
G1-211.p3: Print the PDF free and, if you can, set a few real coins next to the page — matching pictures to metal makes the values stick faster. Mental math within 20 strengthens the adding that money totals depend on, and picture word problems give those coin-counting skills little stories to live in.

G1-212.h1: Draw the Clock Hands to Show the Time
G1-212.title: Draw the Clock Hands for Grade 1 | Free Printable PDF
G1-212.metaDescription: Draw the clock hands worksheet: read each digital time and draw the hour and minute hands on the empty clock face. Free printable Grade 1 time PDF.
G1-212.p1: This Grade 1 telling time worksheet flips the usual clock task on its head. Instead of reading a clock, the child gets four empty clock faces, each paired with a digital time chip. They read the digital time, then draw the hour hand and the minute hand in the right places on the face — short hand for the hour, long hand for the minutes, each exactly where it belongs.
G1-212.p2: Drawing the hands is harder — and more revealing — than reading them. To place the hands correctly, a child must truly understand how a clock works: that the minute hand sweeps the numbers in five-minute jumps, and that the hour hand creeps between numbers as the hour wears on. Translating from digital to analog also connects the two time formats children live with every day, and any misunderstanding shows up instantly in the drawing, which makes this a teacher's favorite quick check.
G1-212.p3: The worksheet prints free as a PDF — handy for a fresh round whenever the times need changing up. It pairs naturally with mental math within 20, since five-minute counting leans on the same skip-counting muscles, and a symmetry drawing page offers more of the careful, precise pencil work this sheet rewards.

G1-213.h1: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems with Pictures
G1-213.title: Word Problems for Grade 1 – Add & Subtract | Free Printable PDF
G1-213.metaDescription: Addition and subtraction word problems with picture support and a dot-grid work space. Two fruit stories to read and solve. Free printable Grade 1 PDF.
G1-213.p1: This Grade 1 word problems worksheet tells two small fruit stories — the kind where someone has a handful of apples and gains or gives away a few more. Under each story, a strip of fruit icons restates the math in pictures, so the child can literally count what the words describe. They read the story, lean on the icons as much as they need to, work things out on the dot-grid panel, and write the answer in the box.
G1-213.p2: Word problems are where arithmetic meets reading, and that meeting is exactly the point. The child must find the question hiding inside the sentences, decide whether the story is asking them to add or to subtract, and only then compute. The picture strip is the bridge: children who are not yet fluent readers can still reason through the mathematics, and the dot grid invites drawings and jottings instead of demanding bare mental work.
G1-213.p3: Print the PDF free and let the child retell each story aloud before solving — hearing the problem is half of understanding it. Fact family houses reinforce how the addition and subtraction in these stories relate to each other, and mental math within 20 builds the quick facts that make word problems feel easy.

G2-251.h1: Column Addition and Subtraction Without Regrouping
G2-251.title: Column Addition and Subtraction Grade 2 | Free Printable PDF
G2-251.metaDescription: Column addition and subtraction worksheet without regrouping: six stacked problems with tidy place-value boxes. Free printable Grade 2 math PDF.
G2-251.p1: This Grade 2 column addition and subtraction worksheet presents six problems stacked vertically, each with place-value boxes that keep the ones under the ones and the tens under the tens. None of the problems needs regrouping, so the child can concentrate entirely on the method itself: start with the ones column, add or subtract, write the digit in its box, then move left and do the same with the tens.
G2-251.p2: The column method is the first genuinely formal procedure most children learn, and it deserves a gentle introduction. Working without regrouping first lets the routine — right to left, one column at a time, one digit per box — become automatic while every individual step still feels easy. The place-value boxes are quiet insurance: they prevent the crooked-column errors behind most early mistakes and keep reinforcing that the 4 in 43 really means four tens. Once this rhythm is second nature, carrying and borrowing have a solid place to land.
G2-251.p3: The sheet prints free as a PDF, perfect for steady weekly practice. When six-for-six becomes routine, addition and subtraction with regrouping is the natural next step up, and mental math practice keeps the small facts fast so the column work stays smooth.

G2-252.h1: Capacity and Mass: Read the Jugs and Scales
G2-252.title: Capacity and Mass Worksheet Grade 2 | Free Printable PDF
G2-252.metaDescription: Capacity and mass worksheet: read three measuring jugs in milliliters and three balance scales in grams, then write each amount. Free Grade 2 PDF.
G2-252.p1: This Grade 2 measurement worksheet splits its page between capacity and mass, with a vehicles theme rolling through it. On one side, three measuring jugs hold liquid at different levels, and the child reads each scale to write the amount in milliliters. On the other, three balance scales weigh little vehicles, and the child reads off each mass in grams. Six readings in all, each one written down together with its unit.
G2-252.p2: Reading a scale is a skill of its own, separate from arithmetic: the child has to work out what each unlabeled tick mark is worth, follow the liquid level or the pointer to the right line, and report the number with its unit attached. Milliliters and grams also give children their first working feel for metric measurement — how much a jug really holds, how heavy a small object really is — turning abstract units into physical intuition they will use in science class and in the kitchen.
G2-252.p3: Print the PDF free and follow up in the real world: a kitchen scale and a measuring cup turn this page into a hands-on afternoon. Column addition and subtraction handles the computation side of measurement work, and reading comprehension keeps the same careful-reading habit growing.

G2-253.h1: Symmetry Drawing: Complete the Mirror Picture
G2-253.title: Symmetry Drawing Worksheet Grade 2 | Free Printable PDF
G2-253.metaDescription: Symmetry drawing worksheet: mirror four pixel-grid pictures across the coral line, square by square. Free printable Grade 2 geometry PDF for kids.
G2-253.p1: This Grade 2 symmetry worksheet shows four pictures made of colored squares on a pixel grid — but each picture is only half finished. A coral line runs through the middle as the mirror. The child studies the completed half, finds each colored square's mirror position on the other side of the line, and colors it in, square by square, until both halves of the picture match perfectly.
G2-253.p2: Completing a mirror image square by square is geometry you can touch. The child discovers that a reflection keeps distances — a square two steps from the line reflects to exactly two steps on the other side — and that left and right swap while up and down hold still. That is genuine spatial reasoning, practiced with a crayon. The grid also demands precision: one miscounted square breaks the whole symmetry, so careful checking becomes part of the game rather than a chore.
G2-253.p3: The worksheet prints free as a PDF, and finished pictures are worth displaying — symmetry looks good on a classroom wall. Children who enjoy the pixel work often love color by code pictures too, and drawing the clock hands offers another dose of the same precise, look-carefully pencil control.

G2-254.h1: Reading Comprehension: Read the Story, Answer the Questions
G2-254.title: Reading Comprehension for Grade 2 | Free Printable PDF
G2-254.metaDescription: Reading comprehension worksheet: a short original story with three multiple-choice questions to circle. Free printable Grade 2 PDF for young readers.
G2-254.p1: This Grade 2 reading comprehension worksheet keeps things beautifully simple: one short original story and three multiple-choice questions about it. The child reads the story carefully — twice is even better — then circles the best answer to each question, going back into the text whenever they are not sure. One story, three questions, and a real conversation waiting to happen afterward.
G2-254.p2: Comprehension is the whole point of learning to read, and it needs its own practice beyond decoding. Three well-aimed questions push the child to do the real work of a reader: recall what happened, connect details across sentences, and choose between answers that all sound plausible until you check the text. The circle-the-answer format keeps writing demands out of the way, so a child whose handwriting is still slow can show full understanding — and the habit of returning to the story for evidence is one of the most valuable reading behaviors there is.
G2-254.p3: Print the PDF free and make the follow-up conversation part of the routine: asking how do you know? turns three questions into a genuine reading lesson. Picture word problems apply the same careful reading to math stories, and number words keeps written-number reading sharp on the side.

G3-357.title: Regrouping Addition and Subtraction Grade 3 | Free Printable PDF
G3-357.metaDescription: Addition and subtraction with regrouping: six column problems with carry boxes for careful carrying and borrowing. Free printable Grade 3 math PDF.
G3-357.p1: This Grade 3 regrouping worksheet brings the column method up to full strength with six problems that all require carrying or borrowing. The addition problems come with carry boxes above the columns, giving the regrouped ten an official home instead of a squeezed-in scribble. The child works right to left — ones first, then tens — regrouping wherever a column overflows or comes up short.
G3-357.p2: Regrouping is where place value stops being a vocabulary word and starts being a tool. Carrying means recognizing that ten ones are worth one ten; borrowing means unbundling a ten back into ones — and a child who can do both, and explain why, genuinely understands how our number system works. The carry boxes matter more than they look: recording the regrouped digit in a fixed spot keeps working memory free for the arithmetic itself and makes every error easy to find and fix afterward.
G3-357.p3: The sheet prints free as a PDF and rewards a slow start: talk through the first problem out loud, then let the remaining five run on their own. If regrouping wobbles, column addition and subtraction without regrouping rebuilds the routine underneath; if it holds solid, times tables practice opens the next chapter of fluency.

G3-358.h1: Times Tables Practice: Twelve Multiplication Facts
G3-358.title: Times Tables Practice for Grade 3 | Free Printable PDF
G3-358.metaDescription: Times tables worksheet: twelve mixed multiplication facts to answer for instant recall. Free printable Grade 3 PDF for daily fact fluency practice.
G3-358.p1: This Grade 3 times tables worksheet lines up twelve multiplication facts and keeps the task perfectly clean: multiply, and write each product in its box. No pictures to decode, no multi-step directions to follow — just the child, the facts, and twelve boxes to fill. A page like this takes only minutes, which is exactly what makes it easy to do often.
G3-358.p2: Times tables are the vocabulary of upper-elementary math. Long multiplication, division, fractions, and area all assume the facts are simply there, ready on demand — and a child who still counts up to reach 7 × 8 spends attention that harder problems need. A short mixed drill builds exactly that instant recall, and because it is only twelve facts, it stays a sprint rather than a slog. Repeated regularly, it also shows progress the child can genuinely feel: fewer pauses this week than last.
G3-358.p3: Print the PDF free and make it a friendly routine — same time each day, no stopwatch pressure required, just steadily smoother recall. Addition and subtraction with regrouping keeps the written methods advancing in parallel, and mental math within 20 keeps the plus-and-minus facts every bit as fast as the times tables. Fluency grows in small, cheerful doses, and this page is exactly one dose.
